result.title: Sequence Composition in EHR Foundation Model Pretraining
result.summary: Autoregressive electronic health record (EHR) foundation models predict the next event token in patient trajectories: sequences of structured medical events. A typical pretraining strategy is to concatenate all trajectories into a global stream and sample token windows from it. This gives patients with longer sequences more training exposure and allows tokens to attend across patient boundaries. We argue that these choices create a misalignment between pretraining and downstream clinical tasks. To explore this, we investigate how the composition of pretraining sequences affects clinical prediction performance. Using the global-stream approach as a baseline, we propose alternative sequence composition methods that control how patient trajectories contribute to pretraining sequences. Across four MIMIC-IV v2.2 tasks, our best method improves macro AUROC, AUPRC, F1, and balanced accuracy, with relative gains of 9.3% in F1 and 2.7% in AUPRC under a fixed training recipe. We find that these gains generalize across four additional evaluation settings, including the INSPIRE and eICU-CRD datasets, with improvements in macro AUROC, AUPRC, and F1 score. Our results show that simply changing how EHR data are presented to the model during pretraining can improve downstream performance, without changing the model or collecting additional data.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 EHR 基础模型预训练中训练序列的组成方式——患者轨迹如何拼接成 token 窗口、是否允许跨患者注意力——并提出可控制各轨迹贡献程度的组合方法与全局流基线对比，在 MIMIC-IV 等任务上取得提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 序列组合方式与跨边界注意力是否泄漏，可能为 LVR 中推理轨迹训练数据的组织、状态监督与贡献分配提供可核查线索；但该工作属 EHR 领域，能否迁移到 VLM 推理训练仍需人工判断。
